title: Zoo or False
cn: 第 19 集 · 动物园还是谎言
novel:
Marshall stumbled into the bar, [[bruised|bruise]] and shaking. "I was [[mugged|mug]]," he said. "By a [[monkey|monkey]]."

The gang stared. "A monkey?" Ted said. "In New York?"

Marshall [[insisted|insist]]. He described the [[attack|attack]] in vivid detail — the tiny hands, the [[screech|screech]], the stolen wallet.

No one believed him. Barney [[suspected|suspect]] Marshall had been beaten up by a child and was too [[ashamed|ashamed]] to admit it. Robin thought he had fallen and invented the monkey to save [[face|face]].

A long [[debate|debate]] followed. Had the monkey escaped from the zoo? Was Marshall lying? Ted, meanwhile, made an [[impulsive|impulsive]] decision to buy a new [[apartment|apartment]], adding to the chaos.

In the end, the truth was never [[confirmed|confirm]]. Marshall clung to his story, and the gang let him. Some [[tales|tale]], Ted realized, mattered less for their truth than for the [[dignity|dignity]] they gave the teller. If a monkey helped Marshall sleep, then a monkey it was.

bruise.en: marked with purple marks from a blow

mug.en: to attack someone in the street and steal from them

monkey.en: an animal similar to a small ape

insist.en: to say firmly that something is true

suspect.en: to think something is true, without being sure

ashamed.en: feeling bad about something you did

face.en: the respect that others give you

debate.en: a discussion where people argue sides

apartment.en: a set of rooms to live in

confirm.en: to prove that something is true

tale.en: a story, often one that may not be true

dignity.en: a calm quality that earns respect
